entries.he: אמר רבא: רב אידי אסברא לי: ״אמרו צדיק כי טוב כי פרי מעלליהם יאכלו״ – וכי יש צדיק טוב ויש צדיק שאינו טוב? אלא: טוב לשמים ולבריות – זהו צדיק טוב, טוב לשמים ורע לבריות – זהו צדיק שאינו טוב. כיוצא בדבר אתה אומר: ״אוי לרשע רע כי גמול ידיו יעשה לו״. וכי יש רשע רע ויש שאינו רע? אלא: רע לשמים ורע לבריות – הוא רשע רע, רע לשמים ואינו רע לבריות – זהו רשע שאינו רע.
entries.en: Rava said: Rav Idi explained to me: “Say of the righteous that he is good, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.” Is there a righteous person who is good and one who is not good? Rather, one who is good toward Heaven and toward people is a good righteous person; one who is good toward Heaven but bad toward people is a righteous person who is not good. Similarly: “Woe to the wicked who is bad, for the recompense of his hands shall be done to him.” Is there a wicked person who is bad and one who is not bad? Rather, one who is bad toward Heaven and toward people is a bad wicked person; one who is bad toward Heaven but is not bad toward people is a wicked person who is not bad.
entries.context: This is the Talmudic distinction between conduct toward Heaven and conduct toward other people. Rav Tzadok applies that distinction here, then expressly limits personal judgment by noting Elisha’s punishment and the danger of self-interest.

entries.en: “Take care lest you offer your burnt offerings.” You are not permitted to do so after it [the Temple] has been built. But one can build an altar as Elijah did on Mount Carmel. From where did Elijah learn to do this on Mount Carmel? From what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Yaakov: “A nation and an assembly of nations shall come from you.” A descendant of Binyamin would arise who would act before an assembly of nations: he would build an altar during the prohibition of private altars, and I would accept it.
entries.context: The Midrash traces Elijah’s exceptional act on Mount Carmel to the words spoken to Yaakov. It begins with the prohibition of private altars; the passage concerns the particular prophetic act, rather than a general permission.

entries.heAnchorPrefix: וְזָכָה לְפִי שְׁנַיִם מֵאֵלִיָּהוּ, כִּי יוֹתֵר יֵשׁ לִפְעוֹל עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה.
entries.he: אף אלישע אדם גדול היה, את מוצא שכל הניסים שעשה אליהו, אלישע עשה כפלים, שנאמר ויהי נא פי שנים ברוחך אלי (מ"ב ב ט), ובא לו שעה ולא ידע כלום, אימתי כשראה השונמית באת אצלו, אמר לגחזי רוץ נא לקראתה וגומר (שם ד כו), ולא ידע שמת הילד בסוף הרגיש ואמר לגחזי הרפה לה כי נפשה מרה לה וה' העלים ממני ולא הגיד לי (שם שם כז). הרי למדת שהכל מן הקב"ה, אם ביקש ראו בני אדם, ואם ביקש שמעו, דכתיב אוזן שומעת ועין רואה ה' עשה גם שניהם (משלי כ יב) לכך נאמר האומר לחרס וגו'.
entries.en: Elisha too was a great man. You find that all the miracles Elijah performed, Elisha performed twice over, as it is stated: “Let there be a double portion of your spirit upon me.” Yet a time came when he knew nothing. When was this? When he saw the Shunammite woman coming to him, he said to Gehazi, “Run now to meet her,” and he did not know that the child had died. In the end he understood and said to Gehazi, “Let her be, for her soul is bitter, and Hashem has hidden it from me and has not told me.” You have learned that everything comes from the Holy One, blessed be He: if He wishes, people see; if He wishes, they hear. As it is written, “The hearing ear and the seeing eye—Hashem made them both.” Therefore it says, “Who commands the sun, and it does not shine.”
entries.context: The Midrash explicitly states that Elisha’s miracles were doubled. It also retains the essential qualification that prophetic knowledge and power depend entirely on God; Elisha was not independently all-knowing.

entries.he: הָאֶחָד — הַחַיּוּת הַמְלֻבָּשׁ בַּגּוּף, שֶׁעָלָיו יִצְדַּק מִיתָה בְּמוֹת הַגּוּף, וְיֵשׁ לְחַיִּים אֵלּוּ גְּבוּל בְּמִדַּת יָמָיו, שֶׁכָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו יֵשׁ לוֹ חַיּוּת זֶה שֶׁל הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַשּׁוֹפַעַת בַּגּוּף, שֶׁזֶּהוּ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁבְּחַיִּים אֵלּוּ הוּא הַיְגִיעָה דְּמִצְוֹת וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים. וְיֵשׁ עוֹד חַיּוּת הַנִּצְחִי דְּנֶפֶשׁ מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ וְלֹא מִצַּד הִתְלַבְּשׁוּתָהּ בַּגּוּף, וּמִצַּד עַצְמָהּ אֵין בָּהּ חִסָּרוֹן שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לַעֲבוֹדָה דִּתְפִלָּה; רַק קוֹל תּוֹרָה הוּא "חַיֵּי עוֹלָם שֶׁנָּטַע בְּתוֹכֵנוּ" [בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה], שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֵסֶק הַצַּדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה; דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא נִבְרָא בְּיוֹ״ד [מְנָחוֹת כ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳], הוּא עַיֵּן שָׁם [עֶצֶם] הַחָכְמָה כַּנּוֹדָע, וְעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּהֵ״א [שָׁם], הוּא הֵ״א תַּתָּאָה הָרוֹמֵז לִתְפִלָּה כַּנּוֹדָע. וְעִקָּר הוּא וַדַּאי הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת שָׁם [י׳ עַמּוּד א׳]): מַנִּיחִים חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִין בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה! רַק מִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם זֶה אֱמֶת דִּבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר שָׁם: דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְחוּד [וּדְבָרֵי תְפִלָּה לְחוּד]; כִּי בֶאֱמֶת: "רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה — יִרְאַת ה'" [תְּהִלִּים קי״א:י׳], וְ"אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ — אִין" [שַׁבָּת ל״א עַמּוּד ב׳], כִּי יְגִיעָה דְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה הֲכָנָה לִזְכּוֹת לְחַיֵּי עוֹלָם, כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשְׁנָה ט״ז): הַתְקֵן עַצְמְךָ בַּפְּרוֹזְדּוֹר וְכוּלֵי, וּ"מִי שֶׁלֹּא טָרַח בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי" [עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳].
entries.en: The first is the vitality clothed in the body, to which death applies when the body dies. These lives have a limit in the measure of one’s days: throughout one’s life, one has this vitality of the soul flowing into the body. This is the life of this world, in which there is the effort of mitzvot and good deeds. There is also the soul’s eternal vitality in itself, apart from its clothing in the body. In itself it lacks nothing that would require the service of prayer; rather, the voice of Torah is “eternal life that He planted within us,” which is the occupation of the righteous in this world. The World to Come was created with the letter yod, the essence of wisdom, as is known; this world with the letter heh, the lower heh that alludes to prayer. The principal thing is certainly Torah, as it is said: “They leave eternal life and occupy themselves with temporal life!” Nevertheless, the view stated there that words of Torah have their own time and words of prayer their own time is also true. For “the beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem,” and “if fear of Hashem is his treasure—yes.” The effort of temporal life prepares one to merit eternal life, as it is said: “Prepare yourself in the antechamber,” and “One who did not toil before Shabbat,” and so forth.
entries.context: Rav Tzadok explains the terms “eternal life” and “temporal life,” while affirming the need for both Torah and prayer. The closing qualification makes prayer and fear of Heaven a preparation for Torah’s eternal life.

entries.he: וְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת הוּא נֶגֶד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּנּוֹדָע, וְהוּא דַרְגָּא דִתְפִלָּה (זֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ג׳ מ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳), שֶׁנִּקְרָא "חַיֵּי שָׁעָה" (שַׁבָּת י׳ עַמּוּד א׳), דְּהוּא רַק לְשָׁעָה; אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא חַיִּים, וְהַיְינוּ קְדֻשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁהוּא טְעִימָה לְשָׁעָה מֵחַיֵּי עוֹלָם; טְעִימָה זוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בַּגּוּף מֵחַיֵּי עוֹלָם הוּא עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה, בַּעֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, הוּא מַמְשִׁיךְ חַיֵּי עוֹלָם לְחַיֵּי שָׁעָה, לִהְיוֹת גַּם בִּשְׁעָתוֹ נִקְרָא חַיּוּת. וְאָמְרוּ: "יָפָה שָׁעָה אַחַת בִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה מִכָּל [חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא]" (אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ד׳ מִשְׁנָה י״ז), וְזוֹ הַחַיֵּי שָׁעָה אַחַת דִּתְשׁוּבָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים הוּא דַרְגָּא דְדָוִד, שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (ה׳ עַמּוּד א׳); שֶׁזֶּהוּ מִדַּת הַנּוּקְבָא חֲסֵרָה: "שָׁלֹשׁ הֵנָּה לֹא תִשְׂבַּעְנָה וְגוֹמֵר" [מִשְׁלֵי ל׳:ט״ו], וְאֵין לָהּ שְׂבִיעָה וְקוֹרַת רוּחַ, רַק קוֹרַת רוּחַ וַהֲנָאָה שֶׁלָּהּ הוּא בַּתְּשׁוּקָה: "וְאֶל אִישֵׁךְ תְּשׁוּקָתֵךְ" [בְּרֵאשִׁית ג׳:ט״ז], בַּמַּה שֶּׁמְּבַקֶּשֶׁת הַהַשְׁלָמָה. וְזֶהוּ דַרְגָּא דְדָוִד שֶׁאָמַר: "בַּקְּשׁוּ פָנָיו תָּמִיד" [תְּהִלִּים ק״ה:ד׳], וְכֵן הַרְבֵּה פְסוּקִים, רַק עַל הַבַּקָּשָׁה וּדְרִישָׁה בִּתְמִידוּת יִהְיֶה מְבַקֵּשׁ, כִּי אֵין לוֹ שְׂבִיעָה דִמְצִיאָה כְּלָל לְעוֹלָם כִּי לֹא תִשְׂבַּעְנָה; רַק: "יִשְׂמַח לֵב מְבַקְשֵׁי ה'" [שָׁם], דְּבַבַּקָּשָׁה עַצְמָהּ יֵשׁ לוֹ שִׂמְחָה, וְיָפָה לוֹ מִכָּל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַבָּא; כִּי אָז לֹא יִהְיֶה מָקוֹם לְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וּבַקָּשָׁה, כִּי "הַיּוֹם לַעֲשׂוֹתָם וּמָחָר לְקַבֵּל שְׂכָרָם" [עֵרוּבִין כ״ב עַמּוּד א׳], הַיְינוּ הַשָּׁעָה שֶׁל קוֹרַת רוּחַ דְּיָפָה מִכָּל חַיֵּי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה [אָבוֹת שָׁם], כִּי יִהְיֶה לוֹ קוֹרַת רוּחַ וְנִיחָא תְּמוּר שֶׁעָשָׂה נַחַת רוּחַ לַמָּקוֹם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא "מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ" [תְּהִלִּים י״ט:ח׳], וְיֵשׁ בְּלִמּוּדָהּ נַחַת רוּחַ וְקוֹרַת רוּחַ, דְּלָכֵךְ הוּא חַיֵּי עוֹלָם מַמָּשׁ, כִּי הוּא עַצְמוֹ הַחַיּוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
entries.en: Shabbat corresponds to David the king, peace be upon him, as is known, and it is the level of prayer, called “temporal life,” for it is only for a time. Nevertheless it is life: the holiness of Shabbat is a temporary taste of eternal life. This taste of eternal life within the body in this world comes through prayer, the service of the heart. One draws eternal life into temporal life, so that even its moment is called vitality. They said: “One hour of repentance and good deeds in this world is better than all the life of the World to Come.” This life of one hour of repentance and good deeds is David’s level, for he established the yoke of repentance, as our Sages said in Avodah Zarah. This is the aspect of the feminine, which is lacking: “Three things are never satisfied.” It has no satiety or contentment; its contentment and pleasure lie in longing—“your longing shall be for your husband”—in seeking completion. This is David’s level, as he said, “Seek His face always,” and many similar verses: one continually seeks and searches, for one never attains the satiety of finding. Rather, “Let the heart of those who seek Hashem rejoice”: there is joy in the seeking itself, and it is better for him than all the life of the World to Come. entries.he: כל הנכנסין להר הבית נכנסין דרך ימין ומקיפין ויוצאין דרך שמאל, חוץ ממי שארעו דבר, שהוא מקיף לשמאל. מה לך מקיף לשמאל, שאני אבל, השוכן בבית הזה ינחמך. שאני מנדה, השוכן בבית הזה יתן בלבם ויקרבוך, דברי רבי מאיר. אמר לו רבי יוסי, עשיתן כאלו עברו עליו את הדין. אלא, השוכן בבית הזה יתן בלבך ותשמע לדברי חבריך ויקרבוך:
entries.en: All who enter the Temple Mount enter by the right, go around, and leave by the left, except someone to whom something has happened, who goes around by the left. “Why do you go around by the left?” “Because I am a mourner.” “May He who dwells in this House comfort you.” “Because I am under a ban.” “May He who dwells in this House put it into their hearts to draw you near”—these are Rabbi Meir’s words. entries.en: Three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come. The three kings are Yerovam, Achav, and Menashe. Rabbi Yehuda says: Menashe has a share in the World to Come, as it is stated, “He prayed to Him, and He was entreated by him and heard his supplication, and restored him to Jerusalem to his kingdom.” They said to him: He restored him to his kingdom, but did not restore him to the life of the World to Come. The four commoners are Bilam, Doeg, Achitofel, and Gehazi.
entries.context: This is the Mishnah’s list that Rav Tzadok acknowledges. Its dispute concerns Menashe; Gehazi appears in the list of four commoners. The following source gives the interpretation invoked at the end of the ois.

entries.heAnchorPrefix: מִכָּל מָקוֹם דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת וְכוּלֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ:
entries.he: דורשי רשומות היו אומרים: כולן באין לעולם הבא, שנאמר: ״לי גלעד ולי מנשה ואפרים מעוז ראשי יהודה מחקקי. מואב סיר רחצי על אדום אשליך נעלי עלי פלשת התרועעי״. ״לי גלעד (ולי מנשה)״ – זה אחאב שנפל ברמות גלעד. ״מנשה״ – כמשמעו. ״אפרים מעוז ראשי״ – זה ירבעם דקאתי מאפרים. ״יהודה מחקקי״ – זה אחיתופל דקאתי מיהודה. ״מואב סיר רחצי״ – זה גחזי, שלקה על עסקי רחיצה. ״על אדום אשליך נעלי״ – זה דואג האדומי. ״עלי פלשת התרועעי״ – אמרו מלאכי השרת לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, אם יבא דוד שהרג את הפלשתי והוריש את בניך גת, מה אתה עושה לו? אמר להן: עלי לעשותן ריעים זה לזה.
entries.en: The interpreters of scriptural hints used to say: All of them come to the World to Come, as it is stated: “Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is the strength of My head; Judah is My lawgiver. Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I cast My shoe; over Philistia, shout in triumph.” “Gilead is Mine” is Achav, who fell at Ramot Gilead. “Manasseh” is literal. “Ephraim is the strength of My head” is Yerovam, who came from Ephraim. “Judah is My lawgiver” is Achitofel, who came from Judah. “Moab is My washbasin” is Gehazi, who was afflicted over the matter of washing. “Upon Edom I cast My shoe” is Doeg the Edomite. “Over Philistia, shout in triumph”—the ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, if David comes, who killed the Philistine and caused Your children to inherit Gat, what will You do for him? He said to them: It is for Me to make them friends with one another.
entries.context: The original discussion continues across the page boundary into 105a, where Gehazi is named explicitly. The final exchange also explains the reconciliation with David alluded to in the parallel passages.

entries.heAnchorPrefix: מִכָּל מָקוֹם דּוֹרְשֵׁי רְשׁוּמוֹת וְכוּלֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ:
entries.he: וּפֵירוּשׁ "רְשׁוּמוֹת" הוּא הָרְשִׁימוּ דְּנֶפֶשׁ עַצְמָהּ הַנִּגְלֶה מִכֹּחַ הַפּוֹעֵל שֶׁבַּנִּפְעָל, וְדוֹרְשֵׁי הֵם הָעוֹמְדִים עַל גִּלּוּי וּמַחֲלָצוֹת סוֹד ה' שֶׁבּוֹ; הֵם מְבִינִים מִכֹּחַ גִּלּוּי עוֹמֶק שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית וּדְבוּקָה בֵּאלֹהִים חַיִּים שֶׁאֵין לָהּ שׁוּם נִיתּוּק כְּלָל בְּסוֹף הַכֹּל כְּשֶׁיֵּעָדְרוּ כָּל מִינֵי לְבוּשִׁים דִּבְחִירָה שֶׁהֵם הַכֹּל לְבוּשֵׁי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, מִצַּד עַצְמִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ דְּחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל שֶׁבְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ פְּרָטִית מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הִיא מְקוּשֶּׁרֶת לְגַמְרֵי בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְזֶהוּ כַּפָּרָה עַל כְּרִיתַת הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם גַּם כֵּן.
entries.en: The meaning of “hints” is the imprint of the soul itself, revealed through the power of the agent within the action. Its interpreters are those who grasp the revelation and uncovering of the secret of Hashem within it. Through the revelation of the depth of the Israelite soul’s root and its attachment to the living God, they understand that it has no complete severance at the final end, when all the garments of choice, which are all garments of this world, fall away. From the essence of the soul as a portion of God above, each individual soul of Israel is wholly bound to the blessed God. This also brings atonement for the cutting off of the root, God forbid.
entries.context: This is Rav Tzadok’s explanation elsewhere of “interpreters of hints.” He distinguishes conduct and its consequences in this world from the final revelation of the soul’s underlying root.

entries.he: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (מד.): "מָשָׁל לְאָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי, אָסָא שְׁמֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁהִמְשִׁילוּ חֲטָאִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לָאָדָם כְּקוֹצִים הַסּוֹבְבִים לַשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה, וְאֵינוֹ מֵעֶצֶם הָאָדָם, רַק שֶׁסּוֹבְבִים וּמַקִּיפִים אוֹתוֹ מִצַּד הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת שֶׁל הָאָדָם. אֲבָל מִצַּד עֶצֶם נֶפֶשׁ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי אֵין בּוֹ חֵטְא כְּלָל, רַק הַמַּדְרֵגוֹת בְּמַעֲלַת הַדְּבֵיקוּת – בָּזֶה הַחִלּוּקִים הוּא בְּעֶצֶם הַנְּפָשׁוֹת, שֶׁמִּצַּד קוֹמַת הַיּוֹשֶׁר יֵשׁ מַדְרֵגוֹת בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת.
entries.en: As they said in Sanhedrin: “It is like a myrtle standing among reeds; it is still called a myrtle,” and so forth. They compared the sins surrounding a person to thorns surrounding a rose. They do not come from the person’s essence, but surround and encompass him on the side of his outward extension. From the essence of the Israelite soul, however, there is no sin at all. Differences in the levels of attachment are differences in the souls themselves, for in the upright arrangement there are degrees among souls.
entries.context: Rav Tzadok explains “incidental” through the image of thorns surrounding a plant. The selected passage distinguishes the soul’s essence from its outward conduct and also preserves the qualification that levels of attachment differ.

sourceEvidence.en: As they said in Sanhedrin: “It is like a myrtle standing among reeds; it is still called a myrtle,” and so forth. They compared the sins surrounding a person to thorns surrounding a rose. They do not come from the person’s essence, but surround and encompass him on the side of his outward extension. From the essence of the Israelite soul, however, there is no sin at all. Differences in the levels of attachment are differences in the souls themselves, for in the upright arrangement there are degrees among souls.

entries.he: אבל ודאי מי שנותן שכר למלמד ללמד מה שהם צריכין ומלמדן יש לו שכר גדול בכך והמלמד עצמו פעמים יש לו שכר פעמים אין לו שכר וכן מי שמאכיל עני או חכם לברכו יש לו שכר על כך ויש לו הנאה בכך כברכת אותו עני או אותו חכם: וכן המסעד מקיימי מצות כדי שיוכלו לקיים יש לו שכר על כך ולהם וביותר מי שעוזר עסוקין בתורה ובמצות להפנות לבותם לעסוק בה יש לו שכר והשכ' שיש לו על פעלתו הוא: ומי שמשיא עצמו לקנות שכר חברו בדמים או במתנה לבוז הוא ולעג וכל הון יקר וחמודות אין אדם קונה בו שכר חברו וכן כתוב אם יתן איש כל הון ביתו באהבה בוז יבוזו לו ואמרו חכמים מאי בוז יבוזו לו אמר עולא לא כשמעון אחי עזריה ולא כיוחנן דבי נשיאה אלא כהלל ושבנא דכי אתא רב דימי אמר הלל ושבנא אחי הוו מר עבד פרקמטיא ומר עסק בתורה אמר ליה פלוג דאיפלוג יצאת בת קול ואמרה אם יתן איש את כל הון ביתו באהבה בוז יבוזו לו עכ"ל:
entries.en: Certainly, one who pays a teacher to teach what they need, and the teacher teaches them, receives great reward for this. The teacher himself sometimes receives reward and sometimes does not. Likewise, one who feeds a poor person or a sage so that he will bless him receives reward for this and benefits through that poor person’s or sage’s blessing. One who supports people fulfilling mitzvot so that they can fulfill them receives reward for this, as do they. Especially one who helps those occupied with Torah and mitzvot to free their hearts to engage in them receives reward; the reward he receives is for his own action. But one who persuades himself that he can acquire his fellow’s reward with money or as a gift deserves scorn and ridicule. No precious wealth or treasures enable a person to acquire his fellow’s reward. Thus it is written: “If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly scorn him.” The Sages asked: What is meant by “they would utterly scorn him”? Ulla said: Not like Shimon, the brother of Azaryah, nor like Rabbi Yochanan of the house of the Nasi, but like Hillel and Shevna. For when Rav Dimi came, he said: Hillel and Shevna were brothers. One engaged in business and the other in Torah. He said to him, “Share with me and I will share with you.” A heavenly voice went forth and said: “If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, they would utterly scorn him.”
entries.context: Maharam Alashkar quotes Rav Hai’s response to the proposed transfer or sale of another person’s religious reward. The passage distinguishes that attempted purchase from the reward a person earns through actually enabling Torah study and mitzvot; both sides of the distinction are retained.

entries.en: He [Yitzchak] considered him [Esav] a vessel prepared for holiness, since he had been formed as a firstborn. Although the firstborn had not yet been sanctified, the forefathers fulfilled the whole Torah and he knew that the firstborn would be sanctified in the future. In truth, however, Yaakov took the birthright and the blessings from him, for everything truly belonged to Yaakov. The birthright came first, even though holiness follows blessing, because the birthright at that time was not holiness itself but a preparation for holiness. He had to take all this from Esav indirectly, because from the appearance of this world everything initially seemed to belong to Esav. For this is the order of the world: first darkness and then light, as they said at the beginning of Berakhot.
entries.context: Rav Tzadok distinguishes a preparation for holiness from holiness already acquired in one’s essence. This explains how the earlier transfer of the birthright fits the ois’s argument about what can and cannot be sold.

entries.heAnchorPrefix: וְעַל זֶה הוּא הַגָּלוּת שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קוֹלְטִים אוֹתוֹ.
entries.he: וְכָל חִבּוּרָם עִם הָאֻמּוֹת, בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ, הוּא רַק לִקְלוֹט נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת מֵהֶם. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים פ״ז עַמּוּד ב׳): לֹא גָּלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְוַסְּפוּ עֲלֵיהֶם גֵּרִים, וְלָאו דַּוְקָא גֵּרִים בַּפֹּעַל, רַק הוֹסָפַת קְלִיטַת כֹּחוֹת הָעַמִּים לְהַחֲזִירָם אֶל הַקְּדֻשָּׁה לְאַט לְאַט, עַד בּוֹא עֵת קֵץ שֶׁיָּשׁוּב הַכֹּל לִקְדוּשָׁה. וְאַף שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת אֵין זֶה גִּלּוּי עֲדַיִן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם בִּפְנִימִיּוּת הַלֵּב אוֹר זֶה גָּלוּי וּמֵאִיר הֵיטֵב, וּפוֹעֵל פְּעֻלָּתוֹ מִכָּל מָקוֹם.
entries.en: All their association with the nations, in its deepest truth, is only to absorb holy sparks from them. As the Sages said: Israel went into exile only so that converts would be added to them. This does not mean only actual converts, but the additional absorption of the nations’ powers, returning them little by little to holiness, until the final time when everything returns to holiness. sourceEvidence.en: All their association with the nations, in its deepest truth, is only to absorb holy sparks from them. As the Sages said: Israel went into exile only so that converts would be added to them. This does not mean only actual converts, but the additional absorption of the nations’ powers, returning them little by little to holiness, until the final time when everything returns to holiness. Although this is not yet revealed outwardly, in the inward heart this light is revealed and shines clearly, and nevertheless accomplishes its work.
